findings.message: The fruit panel closes on the same tick that the reserved and cast-off interruptions happen, so the page never shows those two reasons. When a grapple lands or the ship casts off, MatchRoom.mirrorObjectives passes no pedestal to mirrorFruit (moored needs !held and a dock). status.pedestal becomes "" on the tick the room records fruitResult 'interrupted:reserved' or 'interrupted:released'. FruitPanel.update (apps/web/src/fruitPanel.ts) then closes the panel because !canInspect(status). fruit-message is the only place resultLine is rendered, so 'A duel interrupted your meal' and 'You cast off: eating stopped' never reach the player. The resultLine cast-off branch (coverage row 63) can only run in unit tests. The arena taking over the screen, or the ship sailing off, makes the cause obvious, so the impact is low. Fix: keep the panel's last message visible after it closes, for example on a HUD line.
findings.requirement: The panel shows why an attempt was refused or interrupted (`taken`, `already-eaten`, `empty`, `reserved`, `disconnected`).

findings.message: Keeping the inspecting F press held down starts eating with no second press. FruitPanel.keydown (apps/web/src/fruitPanel.ts) sets held = true for any KeyF keydown while the panel is open, and it checks event.repeat only on the closed-panel path. Once the fruit-kit reply opens the panel, the browser's auto-repeat keydowns (repeat: true) from the same press turn on Buttons.Fruit, and the fruit, which can't be undone for the match, is eaten about 3.5 s after the first press. This contradicts the unit test's own comment 'The press that inspected does not eat; the next one, held, does.' Neither the test nor Playwright's keyboard.down produces auto-repeat. Fix: ignore repeat keydowns unless F is already held, or ignore F until a keyup follows the inspecting press.
findings.requirement: Holding F for 3 s from the panel eats it, with a progress ring.

findings.message: receiveOpenRuin (apps/server/src/MatchRoom.ts) no longer checks island === null. It casts presenceOf(...).island to number and passes a null island into openRuin, whose OpenRuinRequest type says island: number. Behaviour is correct today only because the pure module checks isIsland at runtime ('invalid-request', no clue, state unchanged) and the clue schema rejects a null clue, which the new open-water test confirms. Still, the cast hides a type mismatch across the module boundary, and receiveAnswerRuin in the same file keeps an explicit null branch. A typed guard, or a row marked tested instead of 'removed', would have met the carried item without the cast.
findings.requirement: a room-level test shows that an open-ruin from open water sends no clue. Replace the `equivalent` row in `docs/ruins-online-coverage.md` with it.
